speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long you've had this swelling and if you experienced any injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteochondritis Dissecans (OCD) secondary to a genetic predisposition (e.g., hereditary multiple exostoses or isolated OCD susceptibility). The patient is an 18-month-old male with spontaneous right knee swelling, no traumatic history, and a family history of similar joint issues. This presentation is atypical for standard traumatic OCD; spontaneous onset in a toddler with familial recurrence strongly suggests a developmental or genetic etiology affecting subchondral bone integrity. I will request MRI imaging to confirm subchondral bone lesion and joint stability.
